research.job_description_summary: Goldman Sachs hires engineering analysts in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Two LeetCode Discuss accounts (undated; one from a 2023 graduate) describe a HackerRank assessment (one easy and one medium problem), a CoderPad screen (cycle length in an array, number of islands, a coin-collection matrix) and a Superday of four rounds (DSA twice, software engineering practices or low-level design such as a traffic light system, and a hiring manager round). The official careers page was not fetched.
limitations: Goldman Sachs' official careers page was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.
Both candidate accounts are from LeetCode Discuss and show no posting date; one is explicitly from a 2023 graduate and may predate the 2025 recency window. Treat all class B items as low-confidence.
Problem texts are paraphrased from the accounts' titles and descriptions; statements and test data are original.
The Analyst title in one post's label differs from its body; the role is treated as the Engineering analyst (software) track.
A third post (1.5 YOE) and an Associate post were excluded as experienced hires. Glassdoor reviews found were not India-specific and were not used.
Behavioral items rest on one account; the salary-confidentiality scenario is that single report.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
